t: The Sun Huo Wan Pao Life Evening News

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch
REPORT
File No D. 7738
Date January 21 1937.

Subject The "Sun Huo wan Pao" ("Life Evening News")

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I.S. ROOM

The "Sun Huo wan Pao" ("Life Evening News" 生活晚報),
Lane 226, Burkill Road, is published and edited by Woo Nung Hwe
(吳農花), assisted by Ki Zau Tseng (吉兆徵), formerly
a member of the editorial staff of the defunct "Chen Pao"
("Shanghai Morning Post" 晨報), and Tsang Sin Ts (張恂子),
a mosquito paper journalist.

Mr. Albert A. Favacho, alleged publisher of the
"Sun Huo Wan Pao", resides together with his parents, Mr. and
Mrs. G.R. Favacho, at No. 260 North Szechuen Road. He received
his education in the Assumption College, Bangkok, Siam. From
1917 to 1924 he worked for the Laou Kung Mow Cotton Mill,
Yangtsepoo Road. When the mill closed down, he proceeded to
Bangkok and returned to Shanghai sometime later and in 1931
joined the firm of T.K. Chang and Co., manufacturers of electric
bulbs. In consequence of the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in January 1932, his services were dispensed with.
Recently he was introduced to one M.H. Woo who, he believed,
was a well known Chinese newspaperman. An arrangement was
reached whereby Mr. A.A. Favacho would lend his name to be
used as publisher of a Chinese newspaper to be known as the
"Sun Huo Wan Pao" for a consideration of $50 a month. His duties
were to take care of the outside business of the paper; he was
not to interfere in any fashion whatever with the policy of the
paper. Mr. Favacho says that an agreement was drawn up and
an application for the registration of the paper forwarded to
the Portuguese Consulate, 1650 Rue Lafayette. Prior to registra-
tion being granted, the Consulate stipulated that articles of a
political nature affecting China or Portugal must not be published.

日期 1937年1月21日。

主题 《生活晚报》（"Sun Huo wan Pao"）

由中央情报室制作并转发

《生活晚报》（"Sun Huo Wan Pao"），地址为伯基路（Burkill Road）226弄，由吴农花（Woo Nung Hwe）出版并编辑，吉兆徵（Ki Zau Tseng，已停刊的《晨报》前编辑部成员）和张恂子（Tsang Sin Ts，小报记者）协助。

阿尔伯特·A·法瓦乔（Albert A. Favacho）先生，据称为《生活晚报》的出版人，与其父母G.R.法瓦乔先生和夫人同住于四川北路260号。他曾在暹罗曼谷的圣母书院（Assumption College）接受教育。1917年至1924年间，他在杨树浦路的劳公茂纱厂工作。该厂倒闭后，他前往曼谷，随后不久返回上海，并于1931年加入制造电灯泡的张通和公司（T.K. Chang and Co.）。由于1932年1月中日敌对行动爆发，他被解雇。最近，经人介绍结识了一位名叫M.H. Woo的人士，他认为此人是一位知名的中国报人。双方达成协议，A.A.法瓦乔先生同意出借其姓名作为一份名为《生活晚报》的中文报纸的出版人，每月酬金50美元。他的职责是处理报纸的外部业务；他不得以任何方式干涉报纸的方针。法瓦乔先生称，双方起草了一份协议，并将报纸注册申请提交至霞飞路1650号的葡萄牙领事馆。在准予注册之前，领事馆规定不得刊登涉及中国或葡萄牙的政治性质文章。法瓦乔先生作出必要保证后，注册

was effected and a certificate issued. With the issuance
of this certificate the paper is practically immune from
interference by the Chinese Censorship Bureau and any person
having a complaint to make against the journal would have to
make it against Favaoho, as publisher, in the Portuguese
Consulate.
According to Mr. Favaoho, the capital of the paper is
$5,000. He admits that he has never had any experience of
Chinese newspaper work. His object in entering into a working
agreement with the man Woo was simply to help him secure and
publish plenty of news.
Mr. Braga, Chancellor of the Portuguese Consulate,
upon being interviewed, said that registration was granted
on the following understanding :-
1. That the object of the registration was to enable the
newspaper to publish news ahead of other journals because
foreign registration would render the paper immune from
censorship.
2. That nothing of a political nature concerning China or
Portugal or any other country would appear in the new paper.
On January 18, representations were made by Mr. Tong,
Secretary to Mayor Wu Teh Chen, and later by a representative
of the French Police requesting the cancellation of the
registration on the ground that N.N. Woo was in the habit of
publishing articles derogatory to the Nanking Government and
its officials. As the Portuguese Authorities object to their
citizens meddling in the political affairs of China or of any
other country, Mr. Favaoho was called to the Consulate and
ordered by Mr. Braga, Chancellor, to discontinue publication of

手续得以办理，并颁发了证书。随着该证书的颁发，该报实际上免受中国新闻检查局的干涉，任何对该报刊有投诉的人，都必须向葡萄牙领事馆针对作为出版人的法瓦乔（Favaoho）提出。

据法瓦乔（Favaoho）先生称，该报资本为5,000美元。他承认自己从未有过从事中文报纸工作的经验。他与吴氏达成工作协议的目的，仅仅是为了帮助其获取并发布大量新闻。

葡萄牙领事馆秘书布拉加（Braga）先生在接受问询时表示，注册是基于以下谅解予以批准的：
1. 注册的目的是使该报能够比其他刊物更早发布新闻，因为外国注册将使该报免受审查。
2. 新报纸上不会出现任何涉及中国、葡萄牙或其他国家的政治性质内容。
1月18日，吴铁城市长秘书童先生，以及后来法国警察的代表提出交涉，要求撤销注册，理由是N.N.吴习惯刊登诋毁南京政府及其官员的文章。由于葡萄牙当局反对其公民干涉中国或任何其他国家的政治事务，法瓦乔（Favaoho）先生被召至领事馆，并由秘书布拉加先生命令停止出版

document was returned to the Portuguese Consulate on January 20,
1937.
Mr. Braga also mentioned that his attention had been
drawn to an objectionable article concerning a General Liu
which appeared in the issue of January 18.
An examination of the paper was made by S.5 and an
article was found dealing with General Liu Chung Hwa, Chairman
of the Anhwei Provincial Government, in an unfavourable light.
A curious thing about the article is that the heading read,
"General Liu Shih of Honan Provincial Government", obviously
a mistake. A translation of this article is appended herewith.
The "Sun Huo Wan Pao" appeared as usual on January 19
but the name of Mr. Faracho, the publisher, and the Portuguese
registration, etc. had been deleted.
Woo Hung Hwo(吳震花), publisher and editor of the
"Sun Huo Wan Pao", is notorious for his blackmailing activities.
After severing his connection with the "Holmes"(福尔摩斯), a
mosquito newspaper, he started the "Great Daily News"(大日报)
in 1935.
On January 15, 1936, he was sentenced by the Shanghai
Special District Court to a fine of $30, suspended for two
years, for publishing an indecent article in his paper on
December 14, 1935.
On August 25, 1936, he was fined $200 and his paper
was ordered to be suspended for publishing slanderous articles
against local educational circles. He appealed to the Second
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court and on October 19 the High Court
quashed the original sentences passed by the Court of First

布拉加先生还提到，有人提请他注意1月18日刊载的一篇关于刘将军的不当文章。

第五科对该报进行了检查，发现有一篇文章以不利的角度报道了安徽省政府主席刘仲华（Liu Chung Hwa）将军。该文章的一个奇怪之处在于，标题写的是“河南省政府刘师长”，这显然是一个错误。该文章的译文附后。

《生活晚报》于1月19日照常出版，但出版人法拉乔（Faracho）先生的名字及葡萄牙注册信息等已被删除。

吴震花（Woo Hung Hwo），《生活晚报》的出版人兼编辑，因其敲诈勒索活动而臭名昭著。在与小报《福尔摩斯》断绝关系后，他于1935年创办了《大日报》。

1936年1月15日，他因在其报纸上于1935年12月14日刊登淫秽文章，被上海特区法院判处罚金30美元，缓刑两年。

1936年8月25日，他因刊登诽谤当地教育界的文章，被罚款200美元，并被责令停刊。他向江苏高等法院第二分院上诉，10月19日，高等法院撤销了一审法院的原判决

Instance and imposed on him a fine of $50 only. It was
really an attempt to extort money from a certain school, whose
principal is a member of the executive committee of the local
Tangpu Headquarters. When, instead of receiving hush-money
he sustained a heavy loss, he decided to publish the "Sun Huo
Wan Pao" under foreign protection. He is using the characters
"Sun Huo"("Life") in the name of his paper because newspaper
readers, especially students, are fond of subscribing for
periodicals published by educationalists such as Chow Tao Feng
(鄒奮), Doo Chung Yuan(杜重遠) and Ching Chung Hwa
(金仲華) and bearing such names as "Life Weekly"(生活),
"New Life Weekly"(新生), "Mass Livelihood weekly"(大众生活)
"Perpetual Life Weekly"(永生), etc.
It is reported that Mr. Wong Pei Yuen(王培源), a
lawyer, is helping Woo Hung Hwo in publishing the "Sun Huo Wan
Pao".
According to Mr. Chen Ko Zung, Chief of the local
Newspaper Censorship Bureau, Woo Hung Hwo has neither submitted
a petition to the Shanghai City Government applying for regis-
tration nor has he forwarded to this Bureau proof of reading
matter for censoring.
Continuing, Mr. Chen stated that he sent a letter to
the management of the "National Herald" requesting them to
discontinue the printing of the "Sun Huo Wan Pao" but his
request was disregarded. He intends to ask the Shanghai City
Government to communicate with the Shanghai First Special District
Court to issue instructions ordering the suppression of this
publication.

D. C. (Special Branch)
G. D. I.

，仅对他处以50美元罚款。这实际上是一次向某所学校勒索钱财的企图，该校校长是当地汤浦总部执行委员会的成员。当他不仅未收到封口费反而遭受重大损失时，他决定在外国保护下出版《生活晚报》。他在报名中使用“生活”二字，是因为报纸读者，尤其是学生，喜欢订阅由邹韬奋（Chow Tao Feng）、杜重远（Doo Chung Yuan）和金仲华（Ching Chung Hwa）等教育家出版的、名为《生活周刊》、《新生周刊》、《大众生活周刊》、《永生周刊》等的期刊。

据报道，律师王培源（Wong Pei Yuen）先生正在协助吴震花出版《生活晚报》。

据当地新闻检查局局长陈克忠（Chen Ko Zung）先生称，吴震花既未向上海市政府提交注册申请，也未向该局送交供审查的阅读材料样本。

陈局长接着表示，他曾致函《国民新闻》报社管理层，要求其停止印刷《生活晚报》，但该请求被无视。他打算请求上海市政府与上海第一特区地方法院联系，发出指令取缔该出版物。

D. C. （特务科）
